_doc: Machine-readable era/fault annotations for needle-bench published boards. Referenced by per-board 'faults' lists and boards/index.json. Historical boards publish AS-WERE, clearly era-tagged, and are NEVER re-judged by today's validity rules — these annotations are the honest context a reader needs instead.

faults.title: Published before the fail-closed axis-split validity framework
faults.effect: Cells were not judged for arm receipts, deadlines, stalls, zero-work, or token-accounting integrity; silent drops and rate-card cost synthesis are possible anywhere in these boards. Numbers publish as-were, era-tagged, never re-judged.

faults.title: Gemini streaming cache reads misreported before haystack 073d9154
affects: gemini-* cells in any board generated before 2026-06-16
faults.effect: cachedContentTokenCount was not captured from streaming responses — cache_read under-reported (often 0), so gemini input was priced as fresh and cache columns are untrustworthy for those cells.
faults.reference: haystack 073d9154 fix(gemini-cache): capture streaming cachedContentTokenCount (measurement bug), 2026-06-16

faults.title: June-16 kernel teardown hang — watchdog-scored cells
affects: v7.6.0 june16 snapshot: cells with teardown_masked=true (counted per model/arm in the board's masked columns)
faults.effect: Kernel teardown hung after scoring; the journal+SIGKILL watchdog wrote the score record. The oracle verdict is trusted (test.sh ran to completion) but wall-clock and stop_reason are watchdog artifacts. Cells publish with teardown_masked=true, never silently.

faults.title: July-2 re-run reports cache_read=0 — all input folded into fresh
affects: v7.6.0 july02 snapshot: claude-opus-4-8 native + kernel-cpu, gemini-3.1-pro-preview kernel-cpu
faults.effect: cache_read_tokens/cache_create_tokens are 0 with the whole input total in fresh_input_tokens (billed == fresh). The accounting is real (cost axis VALID) but bucket-split pricing carries no cache discount and the cache columns are not comparable to cache-split snapshots. For real cache buckets use boards/v7.6.0/2026-06-16-experiment-scores.json.

faults.title: arm=None / agent-without-arm-suffix residue (pre arm-receipt fix)
affects: score payloads with a bare '<model>' agent and arm='default', e.g. runs/claude-opus-4-8/off-by-one-pagination.score.json; any June-era board built before arm receipts were enforced
faults.effect: The runner dropped the arm from the agent identity, so the executed arm is unattributable. Under axis-split validity such cells fail the arm-receipt check (no_arm_receipt → fully INVALID on both axes); directories without an arm suffix are not discovered as columns at all. Historical boards that counted them publish as-were with this annotation.

faults.title: claude-fable-5 kernel-cpu refusals — triggered by ostk squashed tool-output format
affects: v7.7.1 july09 snapshot: claude-fable-5 kernel-cpu (18/37 solved, strict-majority; 16 unsolved benches native solved). native arm 34/37.
faults.effect: After 2-3 real tool turns the Anthropic API returns an empty-content response with stop_reason=refusal (journaled as agent exit_code:1); the agent completes without editing, the oracle fails, and the cell records resolved=false with real token accounting (solve+cost axes VALID). This is a provider refusal on the kernel-arm PROMPT SHAPE, not a demonstrated capability gap — treat fable-5 kernel-cpu solve rate as a FLOOR. The 21 cells the kernel DID solve remain honest, and their matched cost vs native holds (kernel = 18% of native cost / 14% of tokens on the 18 both-solved benches).
faults.reference: runs/claude-fable-5-kernel-cpu/*.raw/journal.jsonl (2x cpu.response.decoded stop_reason=refusal per journal); root-cause receipts in the 2026-07-09 bench dossier.
faults.root_cause: Bisected against api.anthropic.com by replaying the exact captured in-container request bodies (OSTK_DUMP_REQUEST). The trigger is ostk's own squasher / gen_table COMPRESSED TOOL-OUTPUT format, cumulatively: two dense squashed tool-results (e.g. '@ostk.prime+0 | v7.7.1 | POST 7/7 ... laws: invisible-write | ephemeral', '[ls_uniform] owner:root:root perms_f:mixed:2 ... [ls_anomaly]') cross Fable 5's dual-use safety threshold; rewriting EITHER result to plain text clears the refusal. Refuted as causes: tool-surface size (trimming to coding-only still refuses) and missing framing (an explicit authorized-benchmark system prompt still refuses). Only reducing squashed-output density clears it. Claude Fable 5 ships additional dual-use safety measures; its classifier reads accumulated cryptic/obfuscation-shaped output (compounded by the terse 'find the needle' prompt) as suspicious. The native arm never hits this because the vendor CLI passes plain tool output.
faults.mitigation: Operator design decision (NOT auto-applied): soften the squasher rendering for Anthropic frontier models (fable/mythos) — the only lever that provably works — or carry a per-model output-format capability flag, or accept+report as-is. Also: some refusal-terminated cells still trip the teardown-hang path because --profile oneshot keys clean exit on end_turn, not refusal; stall_watch SIGKILLs them correctly. A follow-up haystack change could treat refusal as a clean oneshot terminal.

faults.title: claude-opus-4-8 kernel-cpu: agent loop hard-exits on undeclared tool request — 2 cells lost
affects: v7.7.1 july09 snapshot: claude-opus-4-8 kernel-cpu (34/38 raw strict-majority; relaxed-ordering-ringbuf and tls-chain-ordering-strict recorded unsolved). native arm unaffected (35/38).
faults.effect: In 2 kernel-cpu cells the model requested `ostk_show` — an operator-overlay verb that is CLI-only by design (→1589) and correctly absent from the MCP tool surface. Instead of returning an in-band unknown-tool error result, the agent loop journaled the declared_tools listing and hard-exited with code 1, discarding the VALID read/bash tool calls pending in the same content block. Cells record resolved=false with real token accounting (solve+cost axes VALID). This is a kernel harness defect, not a demonstrated capability gap — treat opus-4-8 kernel-cpu solve rate as a FLOOR (observed ceiling ~36/38).
faults.reference: runs/claude-opus-4-8-kernel-cpu/{relaxed-ordering-ringbuf,tls-chain-ordering-strict}.raw/journal.jsonl (cpu.response.decoded stop_reason=tool_use, then declared_tools row + agent.completed exit_code:1).
faults.root_cause: haystack agent-loop unknown-tool handling: a tool_use naming an undeclared tool terminates the agent (exit 1) rather than producing an error tool_result the model can recover from. Amplified by a vocabulary collision: the in-container boot envelope reports `needles: 0 open` (ostk work items) while the bench prompt says 'find the needle' (the planted bug), steering models toward the operator-overlay `show` verb.
faults.mitigation: Scores stand as honest evidence of harness behavior under the v7.7.1 pin. Fix in progress on haystack (in-band unknown-tool error); kernel-arm re-capture of the two cells deferred until the fixed kernel lands in a new content-hash pin — valid cells are never re-rolled on the same binary.

faults.title: F7 resampling stopped on mid-stream solve — [F,T] cells scored 1/2 miss without their deciding sample
affects: v7.7.1 july09 snapshot: claude-opus-4-8 kernel-cpu encoding-mojibake (samples [F,T]); claude-fable-5 kernel-cpu deadlock-transfer and linearizability-stale-read (samples [F,T]). Solve rates for those model-arms are FLOORS (opus-4-8 kernel observed ceiling rises to ~37/38 combined with july09-opus48-unknown-tool-loop-exit).
faults.effect: Two design iterations drifted: the run_matrix F7 loop implemented retry semantics (stop resampling on any resolved sample, canonical score preserved) while consolidate_scores.py:418 scores strict majority over ALL samples taken. A cell that missed sample 1 and solved sample 2 locked in 1/2 = unsolved without ever running the deciding third sample. Cells publish as-were with this annotation.
faults.reference: run_matrix_v41.py F7 outer loop (fixed 2026-07-09: once resampling begins, the full sample budget runs and strict majority decides); consolidate_scores.py:418; truncated-vote scan in the 2026-07-09 bench dossier.
faults.mitigation: Harness fixed 2026-07-09 before the v7.7.2 board was published. claude-sonnet-5 kernel-cpu silent-data-corruption hit the same truncation during capture and was remediated by a cold re-run under the fixed protocol before publish; it solved on sample 1 of the cold run and publishes as SOLVED under the era's uniform sample-1 trust rule. FULL SAMPLE HISTORY for that cell across the three 2026-07-09 captures: [F] (hard-fail bug, archived at runs-archive/sonnet5-kernel-sdc-hardfail-20260709), [F,T] (this truncation bug, archived at runs-archive/sonnet5-kernel-sdc-truncatedF7-20260709), [T] (canonical). 2 solves in 4 samples — the cell is variance-prone; both re-runs were forced by verified harness bugs before their outcomes were known. The two affected fable cells are superseded by the 2026-07-09 fable kernel re-capture; the opus cell publishes as-was (frozen era, archived pin — valid cells are never re-rolled on a different binary).

faults.title: run_cell hard-failed clean completed-but-unsolved exits — unmasked by the v7.7.2 teardown fix
affects: No published board carries a mis-scored cell from this. Transient during v7.7.2 capture: claude-sonnet-5 kernel-cpu silent-data-corruption was classified hard-fail after a clean unsolved exit and denied F7 resampling; remediated by cold re-run before publish (single-sample capture archived at runs-archive/sonnet5-kernel-sdc-hardfail-20260709; see july09-f7-earlystop-truncated-votes for that cell's full sample history).
faults.effect: run_cell required returncode==0 to treat a self-exit as completed, but ostk bench exits 1 by design for a completed-but-unsolved scenario ('error: N scenario(s) failed'). The misclassification was invisible before v7.7.2 because unsolved kernel cells always hung at teardown and took the completed_kill path (scored, teardown_masked); the teardown fix (haystack ebcbe2b0) made clean unsolved exits possible for the first time.
faults.reference: run_matrix_v41.py run_cell completed-gate (fixed 2026-07-09: a self-exit is completed regardless of returncode; the fresh-valid-score gate decides success); haystack ebcbe2b0 fix(bench).
faults.mitigation: Fixed in harness 2026-07-09. Also makes refusal-terminated cells (clean nonzero exits) score correctly for the fable re-capture instead of hard-failing.

faults.title: claude-sonnet-5 native cost axis inflated — vendor CLI prices sonnet-5 at the Opus 4.8 rate card
affects: v7.7.1 july09 snapshot: claude-sonnet-5 native COST axis only (recorded $17.51 total; honest $7.58 at intro rates / $11.36 at standard). Solve axis and token counts unaffected.
faults.effect: estimated_cost_usd is copied from the Claude Code CLI's own telemetry, and the CLI's price table maps claude-sonnet-5 to the Opus 4.8 rate card ($5/$25/$0.50/$6.25 per MTok) instead of Sonnet 5's $2/$10 introductory (through 2026-08-31) / $3/$15 standard — a uniform 2.5x (intro) / 1.67x (standard) overcharge on every sonnet native cell. Proven by exact linear-fit recovery of the CLI's effective rates from all 38 cells (max residual ~1e-15); opus-4-8 and fable-5 recover their genuine published rates (zero delta), so only sonnet-5 is mis-tiered. The long-context-premium hypothesis is disproven (200K window cap, flat-rate fit, docs confirm 1M at standard pricing). One cell (nginx-upstream-port-mismatch) additionally recorded $0 cost despite real tokens.
faults.reference: scripts/reprice_native.py (pinned source-verified rate table, per-model repricing); cost-repricing findings 2026-07-09; runs/claude-sonnet-5-native/*.raw/native.stdout modelUsage.
faults.mitigation: Recorded cells publish as-were with this annotation (cost_basis stays CLI-self-reported). Honest totals are reproducible from raw telemetry via scripts/reprice_native.py. Board-level cost restatement is an operator data-policy decision, deferred to the full clean re-capture.

faults.title: claude-fable-5 native: 4 security cells silently served partly by Opus 4.8 (classifier fallback)
affects: v7.7.1 july09 snapshot: claude-fable-5 native cells auth-bypass-path-traversal, bidi-override-injection, rate-limit-bypass-header, ssrf-allowlist-port-confusion.
faults.effect: Fable 5's cyber-safety classifier tripped mid-session on these security-flavored benches and the vendor CLI silently continued the session on claude-opus-4-8. Raw per-model telemetry (modelUsage) shows three billable models per cell (haiku sidecar + partial fable + opus); the score-file aggregate blends fable+opus tokens into one bucket (verified: auth-bypass fresh 1956 = fable 1815 + opus 141). Solve attribution for these 4 cells is NOT pure fable-5, and any single-rate cost treatment of the aggregate is wrong by construction.
faults.mitigation: Cells publish as-were with this annotation. Handling (annotate-only vs exclude vs re-run) is deferred to the operator's full clean re-capture; the kernel arm is unaffected (single-model by construction).
